title: Time-weighted burst smoothing and respectful eviction controller
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Background: Dedicated fleets serve a mix of steady tenants and bursty tenants. Short, intense bursts are valuable for customer experience but can trigger aggressive preemption/eviction that harms long‑running tenants and causes oscillation. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: a time‑weighted burst credit allocator (TWBCA) that smooths burst consumption over a configurable half‑life, and a respectful eviction controller (REC) that uses the TWBCA signal plus utilization patterns to prefer reclamation from sustained, low‑priority consumers while avoiding immediate eviction for transient overshoot.

What this changes: added a new crediting model: each tenant now accrues a time‑weighted burst balance that decays with a configurable half_life_ms. When a tenant consumes burst tokens, the draw reduces the balance and increases a short lived "burst_pressure" metric. The autoscaler and preemption path consult both current instantaneous utilization and the TW balance to decide whether to trigger preemption. REC computes an eviction_score that mixes (1) normalized sustained utilization, (2) TW balance (higher balance => lower eviction preference), and (3) preemption_cooldown windows to avoid thrash.

Key goals: reduce eviction churn during short bursts, preserve throughput guarantees for committed tenants, and provide predictable telemetry for capacity planning.

Implementation details: - controller/twbca: new loop that samples per-tenant token consumption and updates a compact EWMA state (64b per tenant) stored alongside reservation metadata. Uses integer math in hot path and converts to double only for export. - controller/rec: integrates with existing leasebook and scorecard pipelines. Supports pluggable scoring weights and configurable preemption_window_ms. - config schema changes: added dedicated.twbca.enabled, dedicated.twbca.half_life_ms, dedicated.rec.preemption_window_ms, dedicated.rec.eviction_weight_factors (sustained, burst_balance, cooldown). Defaults are conservative (TWBCA off by default; REC can be enabled cluster‑wide or per‑pool). - telemetry: new metrics exported via prometheus: redwood_dedicated_twb_balance{tenant}, redwood_rec_eviction_score{tenant,pool}, redwood_rec_preemption_cooldown_active{tenant}. Also added histogram redwood_rec_evict_latency_ms. - tests: unit tests for EWMA math, integration tests with synthetic load to validate eviction prioritization, and an end‑to‑end canary harness that runs in perf‑canary repo.

Rollout plan: start with TWBCA disabled by default. Enable REC in a canary dedicated pool for 2 weeks with verbose metrics. If stable, flip TWBCA on with half_life_ms=300000 (5m) for canary, then progressively increase to 15m for tenants with bursty workloads. Document knobs and recommended values in the Dedicated capacity ops runbook.

Checklist:
- [x] EWMA algorithm and math vetted in design doc (ENG-1298)
- [x] Unit and integration tests added
- [x] Metrics and dashboards (DevOps) wired up
- [x] Backwards compatible config with safe defaults
- [x] Release notes drafted

Risks and mitigation: If half_life too short we fall back to prior behavior; if too long we could underreact to actual overcommit and starve low‑priority tenants. Mitigations: conservative defaults, gradual rollout, automatic kill‑switch that reverts to legacy eviction when global eviction_rate > configured threshold.

Related: references the preemption_window work (ENG-2021) for the cooldown gating. Also ties into the per‑tenant telemetry collector work in metrics team to allow capacity planners to set reservation buffers.

Notes on code hygiene: added a feature flag gate and feature toggle in the runtime feature registry. All new exported config keys are documented in the schema and validated in the bootstrap path.

review_conversation: Arun: Can you clarify why EWMA chosen over simple sliding window? Author: EWMA reduces state footprint and avoids expensive window bookkeeping in hot path; documented math in comments.
Sofia: Concern about default off — how will we surface the improvement? Author: added canary dashboard and perf‑canary job to measure eviction churn and tail latency.
Diego: Question on integer math edge cases. Author: added tests for overflow and rounding; moved conversion points out of hot path.
Arun: +1 after addressing race in leasebook read path. Sofia: approved. Diego: approved with minor nits fixed.
release_notes: Introduce time-weighted burst credit allocator (TWBCA) and Respectful Eviction Controller (REC). Default: TWBCA off, REC can be enabled per pool. Adds telemetry: redwood_dedicated_twb_balance, redwood_rec_eviction_score, and associated dashboards. Improves eviction stability during short bursts and provides knobs for operators to tune smoothing and preemption windows.
user_impact: Operational: operators get new telemetry and config knobs; should see reduced eviction churn in canary pools once enabled. Default behavior unchanged until explicitly enabled.
manual_steps: To enable on a pool: set dedicated.twbca.enabled=true and set dedicated.rec.preemption_window_ms=60000 in cluster values, restart controller. Monitor redwood_rec_eviction_score and redwood_rec_evict_latency_ms.
notes: This PR was coordinated with the metrics team to ensure the new per-tenant metrics are high-cardinality safe via a sampling policy. Follow-up work will add aggregated signals used by billing/costing pipelines.
